goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137 — On a failed passkey submission during fresh login, webauthnAuth.action -> createErrorResponse -> errorChallenge re-renders the form via createLoginForm, but the user==null path no longer refreshes the webauthn challenge/attributes, so the retried conditional-UI passkey has no valid AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE and fails.

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm, the logic to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() was changed from the user==null case to only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user!=null). This means any re-render of the username/password form while context.getUser() is still null (e.g., fresh-login conditional/passkey attempts before a user is identified) will no longer populate WebAuthn/passkey form attributes/notes via UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(...). If the passkey error flow re-renders the login form (as described) and the earlier fillContextForm done in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse gets lost when the form is recreated, the follow-up page would indeed miss refreshed challenge state (e.g., AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE), causing retry failures. The diff shows this regression in the null-user path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:65 — shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override lacks @Override, so a future signature change in WebAuthnAuthenticator would silently stop suppressing the allowed-authenticators list during re-authentication.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new protected hook method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` and adds a same-signature method in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` intended to override it and return `false`. Because the override in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` lacks `@Override`, a future signature change in the superclass could cause this method to stop overriding without a compile-time error, potentially re-enabling authenticator list display unintentionally. This is a maintainability/robustness concern, not a current functional defect shown by the diff.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137 — Error challenge path also uses the user != null guard, so after a bad username/password on fresh login the re-rendered form lacks webauthn challenge data and the passkey autofill is silently disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm, both the initial authenticate() render and the error challenge() path now call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true. That helper explicitly requires user != null (and passkeys enabled). On a fresh login (before a user is identified) and after a bad username/password where the flow may clear context.getUser(), this guard prevents fillContextForm from running, so the re-rendered form won’t include the WebAuthn/passkeys context data that previously would have been set when passkeys were enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UsernameForm.authenticate()` is changed to call `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` shown in this PR diff is newly added in `UsernamePasswordForm` as `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which is a different class and a different signature. adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, inverting the previous `user == null` condition so conditional-UI passkeys (and their challenge note) are no longer set up on a normal first-factor login, silently dropping the passwordless option

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context,error,field) from running `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null && passkeysEnabled` (i.e., normal first-factor where user not identified yet) to only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and that helper explicitly requires `user != null`. This is an inversion of the previous condition for the error challenge path, so on an initial login (user null) the passkeys/conditional-UI context setup will no longer run from this form, which can drop the passkey option/challenge data unless something else in the flow sets it up (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:279 — reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey while passkeys are enabled, so the "user has no passkey" re-auth case in the comment is not actually covered.

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the realm is explicitly configured with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so the assertions that the WebAuthn UI (`//form[@id='webauth']`) is absent are satisfied because passkeys are disabled realm-wide, not because the selected user lacks a passkey. This means the test (and its in-body comment "as this user does not have passkey") does not actually exercise the scenario of "passkeys enabled in realm, but this user has no passkey"; it cannot distinguish user-based absence from realm-based absence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:378 — No test covers a failed passkey during re-authentication (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator error path calling setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError), so USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on that path is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior specifically in the passkey failure/error flow: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` now calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note is true. The newly added/modified tests in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` cover re-authentication success with passkeys, password failures during re-auth, and passkeys visibility, but do not exercise a *failed passkey during re-authentication* that would hit this `createErrorResponse` path and thus validate the `USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED` attributes are preserved in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:378 — After wrong password during re-auth the test only checks the error text and webauth form; it never asserts the username stays hidden / registration link absent, which is the behavior the refactored error path is meant to preserve.

adjudication.rationale: The diff refactors the re-authentication error handling into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which explicitly sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is true. In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` the new re-authentication scenario after an incorrect password only asserts the error text (`"Invalid password."`) and that the webauthn form is still present; it does not assert the re-auth UI invariants (username remains hidden / registration disabled) that this refactor is intended to preserve. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for the newly centralized logic, not a product defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:261 — UsernameForm change (no auto-skip when passkeys enabled) is only tested with a discoverable key that auto-logs in; no test shows the username form being rendered on re-auth with an external key, no regression test that the form is still skipped when passkeys are disabled, and no linked-IDP case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() to *not* auto-skip when context.getUser() != null if conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). In the same file’s tests, the only newly added coverage in PasskeysUsernameFormTest is `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, which uses a discoverable key path that auto-logs in and never asserts that the username form is actually rendered/handled during re-authentication. The diff also doesn’t add any UsernameForm-focused regression test for the previous skip behavior when passkeys are disabled, nor any test for the linked-broker (IDP-linked) branch mentioned in the UsernameForm comment. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:293 — try/assertThat(nullValue)/fail/catch(Exception) idiom for "element absent" is convoluted and swallows any WebDriver exception; use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as the sibling test does.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java (added reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test), the diff introduces a try { driver.findElement(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception) { /* expected */ } pattern to assert absence of the webauthn form. This is convoluted and catches any Exception (not just NoSuchElementException), potentially masking unrelated WebDriver/test failures. The sibling tests in this diff use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) for the same purpose, which is more precise.
